category: Scripting: BoundarySetup, MeshSetup, AnalysisSetup, RadField & Optimetrics Modules
description: Native module commands obtained with oDesign.GetModule(...) that define the electromagnetic problem and the studies: the remaining BoundarySetup assignments (Floquet, Perfect H, impedance, layered impedance, lumped RLC, PML, FE-BI, symmetry, lattice pair/master-slave, voltage/current, incident waves, circuit ports, terminals, auto-identification, editing/deleting/querying boundaries), the MeshSetup operations and initial mesh settings, AnalysisSetup setups/sweeps editing and mesh links, RadField near/far-field setups, and Optimetrics parametric/optimisation/sensitivity/statistical setups with solve and export.

tools.name: oModule("BoundarySetup").AssignFloquetPort
tools.description: Assign a Floquet port to a face of a unit cell: number of modes, renormalisation, de-embedding, the modes list, the lattice A and B vectors (start/end points), the reporter filter selecting which modes appear in reports and the scan-angle definition. Used with AssignLatticePair for infinite arrays and frequency-selective surfaces.
tools.usage:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("BoundarySetup")
oModule.AssignFloquetPort(["NAME:FloquetPort1", "Faces:=", [7], "NumModes:=", 2, "RenormalizeAllTerminals:=", True, "DoDeembed:=", True, "DeembedDist:=", "h_air",
    ["NAME:Modes", ["NAME:Mode1", "ModeNum:=", 1, "UseIntLine:=", False], ["NAME:Mode2", "ModeNum:=", 2, "UseIntLine:=", False]],
    "ShowReporterFilter:=", True, "ReporterFilter:=", [True, True], "UseScanAngles:=", True, "Phi:=", "0deg", "Theta:=", "0deg",
    ["NAME:LatticeAVector", "Start:=", ["0mm", "0mm", "0.8mm"], "End:=", ["0mm", "p", "0.8mm"]],
    ["NAME:LatticeBVector", "Start:=", ["0mm", "0mm", "0.8mm"], "End:=", ["p", "0mm", "0.8mm"]]])

parameters.name: Faces
parameters.description: Face ID list of the port face (top or bottom of the cell).

parameters.name: NumModes / Modes
parameters.description: Number of Floquet modes and their definitions (TE00/TM00 specular modes first).

parameters.name: DoDeembed / DeembedDist
parameters.description: Move the reference plane by the given distance along the face normal.

parameters.name: LatticeAVector / LatticeBVector
parameters.description: Start/End points defining the periodicity vectors in the port plane.

parameters.name: ReporterFilter
parameters.description: Booleans per mode - modes with False are excluded from reports/S-matrix.

parameters.name: UseScanAngles / Phi / Theta
parameters.description: Scan direction of the incident Floquet wave (must match the lattice pair phase delay).

tools.example:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("BoundarySetup")
oModule.AssignFloquetPort(["NAME:Floquet", "Faces:=", [int(top_face)], "NumModes:=", 2, "RenormalizeAllTerminals:=", True,
    "DoDeembed:=", True, "DeembedDist:=", "h_air",
    ["NAME:Modes", ["NAME:Mode1", "ModeNum:=", 1, "UseIntLine:=", False], ["NAME:Mode2", "ModeNum:=", 2, "UseIntLine:=", False]],
    "ShowReporterFilter:=", True, "ReporterFilter:=", [True, True], "UseScanAngles:=", True, "Phi:=", "phi_scan", "Theta:=", "theta_scan",
    ["NAME:LatticeAVector", "Start:=", ["-p/2", "-p/2", "h_air"], "End:=", ["p/2", "-p/2", "h_air"]],
    ["NAME:LatticeBVector", "Start:=", ["-p/2", "-p/2", "h_air"], "End:=", ["-p/2", "p/2", "h_air"]]])
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.create_floquet_port(face, lattice_origin, lattice_a_end, lattice_b_end, modes, ...). Use EditFloquetPort(name, array) to modify. The port face must be planar and coincide with the lattice-pair boundary edges.

tools.name: oModule("BoundarySetup").AssignPerfectH / AssignImpedance / AssignLayeredImp
tools.description: Three surface boundaries: Perfect H (magnetic wall) on faces or objects, the isotropic Impedance boundary with resistance and reactance per square and an infinite-ground option, and the Layered Impedance boundary that models a stack of thin layers (material + thickness each) with roughness, one- or two-sided and shell-element options.
tools.usage:
oModule.AssignPerfectH(["NAME:PerfH1", "Faces:=", [12]])
oModule.AssignImpedance(["NAME:Imped1", "Resistance:=", "377", "Reactance:=", "0", "InfGroundPlane:=", False, "Faces:=", [12]])
oModule.AssignLayeredImp(["NAME:Layered1", "Objects:=", ["Rectangle1"], "Frequency:=", "0GHz", "Roughness:=", "0um", "IsTwoSided:=", True, "IsShellElement:=", False,
    ["NAME:Layers", ["NAME:Layer1", "Thickness:=", "1um", "Material:=", "gold"], ["NAME:Layer2", "Thickness:=", "3um", "Material:=", "nickel"]], "InfGroundPlane:=", False])

parameters.name: Objects / Faces
parameters.description: Assignment by object names or face IDs (one of the two).

parameters.name: Resistance / Reactance
parameters.description: Ohms per square as strings; the anisotropic form is AssignAnisotropicImpedance with a 2x2 tensor.

parameters.name: Layers
parameters.description: Ordered from the field side inward; each layer has Thickness and Material.

parameters.name: IsTwoSided / IsShellElement / Roughness
parameters.description: Sheet with fields on both sides, shell-element treatment, and surface roughness value.

tools.example:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("BoundarySetup")
oModule.AssignPerfectH(["NAME:MagWall", "Faces:=", [int(f) for f in top_faces]])
oModule.AssignImpedance(["NAME:Absorber", "Resistance:=", "377", "Reactance:=", "0", "InfGroundPlane:=", False, "Objects:=", ["AbsSheet"]])
oModule.AssignLayeredImp(["NAME:Plating", "Objects:=", ["WGWall"], "Frequency:=", "0GHz", "Roughness:=", "0.5um", "IsTwoSided:=", False,
    "IsShellElement:=", False, ["NAME:Layers", ["NAME:Layer1", "Thickness:=", "1um", "Material:=", "gold"],
    ["NAME:Layer2", "Thickness:=", "1mm", "Material:=", "aluminum"]], "InfGroundPlane:=", False])
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.assign_perfect_h, assign_impedance_to_sheet, assign_layered_impedance. Editing: EditPerfectH / EditImpedance / EditLayeredImpedance(name, array).

tools.name: oModule("BoundarySetup").AssignLumpedRLC
tools.description: Assign a Lumped RLC boundary to a sheet: parallel or serial topology, which of R, L, C are used and their values, and the current line (start/end points on the sheet) that defines the element direction. It models chips, loads, capacitive gaps and matching elements as ideal two-terminal networks.
tools.usage:
oModule.AssignLumpedRLC(["NAME:LumpRLC1", "Objects:=", ["RLCSheet"],
    ["NAME:CurrentLine", "Start:=", ["0mm", "0mm", "0mm"], "End:=", ["0mm", "1mm", "0mm"]],
    "RLC Type:=", "Parallel", "UseResist:=", True, "Resistance:=", "50ohm", "UseInduct:=", False, "Inductance:=", "0nH", "UseCap:=", True, "Capacitance:=", "1pF"])

parameters.name: RLC Type
parameters.description: "Parallel" or "Serial".

parameters.name: UseResist / UseInduct / UseCap
parameters.description: Enable each element; disabled elements are ignored regardless of value.

parameters.name: CurrentLine
parameters.description: Start/End points on the sheet giving the current direction (with units).

parameters.name: Objects / Faces
parameters.description: Sheet name or face ID.

tools.example:
oModule.AssignLumpedRLC(["NAME:Chip", "Objects:=", ["ChipSheet"],
    ["NAME:CurrentLine", "Start:=", ["x_chip", "-w_gap/2", "h_sub"], "End:=", ["x_chip", "w_gap/2", "h_sub"]],
    "RLC Type:=", "Serial", "UseResist:=", True, "Resistance:=", "15ohm", "UseInduct:=", False, "Inductance:=", "0nH",
    "UseCap:=", True, "Capacitance:=", "0.9pF"])
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.assign_lumped_rlc_to_sheet / create_lumped_rlc_between_objects. Edit with EditLumpedRLC(name, array). Values must carry units (ohm, nH, pF).

tools.name: oModule("BoundarySetup").CreatePML
tools.description: Run the PML wizard from a script: either build PML layers automatically on selected faces of the region (with a thickness, the radiating distance, an optional joining of corner objects and a minimum frequency/beta for material design) or turn user-drawn objects into PML with a base object and orientation. The generated PML objects receive graded absorbing materials tuned for the given minimum frequency.
tools.usage:
oModule.CreatePML(["NAME:PMLCreationSettings", "UserDrawnGroup:=", False, "PMLFaces:=", [120, 121, 122], "CreateJoiningObjs:=", True,
    "Thickness:=", "lambda0/4", "RadDist:=", "lambda0/4", "UseFreq:=", True, "MinFreq:=", "1GHz", "MinBeta:=", 20])
oModule.CreatePML(["NAME:PMLCreationSettings", "UserDrawnGroup:=", True, "PMLObj:=", "PMLBox", "BaseObj:=", "Region", "Thickness:=", "10mm", "Orientation:=", "ZAxis",
    "RadDist:=", "20mm", "UseFreq:=", True, "MinFreq:=", "1GHz", "MinBeta:=", 20])

parameters.name: UserDrawnGroup
parameters.description: False = automatic layers on PMLFaces; True = user objects PMLObj/BaseObj with Orientation.

parameters.name: PMLFaces / CreateJoiningObjs
parameters.description: Faces of the region to cover and whether corner/edge PML blocks are generated.

parameters.name: Thickness / RadDist
parameters.description: PML layer thickness and the distance from the radiating structure (both set the material grading).

parameters.name: UseFreq / MinFreq / MinBeta
parameters.description: Design the PML for the lowest frequency of interest with the given minimum propagation constant.

tools.example:
faces = [int(f) for f in oEditor.GetFaceIDs("Region")]
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("BoundarySetup")
oModule.CreatePML(["NAME:PMLCreationSettings", "UserDrawnGroup:=", False, "PMLFaces:=", faces, "CreateJoiningObjs:=", True,
    "Thickness:=", "20mm", "RadDist:=", "30mm", "UseFreq:=", True, "MinFreq:=", "2GHz", "MinBeta:=", 20])
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.create_open_region(frequency, boundary="PML") or hfss.set_auto_open(True, "PML"). PML objects appear as separate objects with PML materials; there is no EditPML command, so changing the region afterwards means deleting the PML objects and running CreatePML again.

tools.name: oModule("BoundarySetup").AssignFEBI / AssignHybridRegion / AssignSymmetry
tools.description: Hybrid and symmetry assignments: FE-BI on objects (exact absorbing boundary through the boundary-integral method), hybrid regions solved by IE, PO or SBR+ instead of FEM, and symmetry planes (Perfect E or Perfect H type) on faces. The hybrid commands require the design's hybrid solution type flag.
tools.usage:
oModule.AssignFEBI(["NAME:FE-BI1", "Objects:=", ["RegularPolyhedron1"]])
oModule.AssignHybridRegion(["NAME:SBR1", "Objects:=", ["Mast"], "Type:=", "SBR+"])      # "IE" / "PO" / "SBR+"
oModule.AssignSymmetry(["NAME:Sym1", "IsPerfectE:=", True, "Faces:=", [12]])
oDesign.SetSolutionType("HFSS Modal Network", ["NAME:Options", "EnableAutoOpen:=", False, "Hybrid:=", True])

parameters.name: Objects
parameters.description: Object names forming the FE-BI/hybrid region.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: Hybrid method for the region: "IE", "PO" or "SBR+".

parameters.name: IsPerfectE
parameters.description: True for Perfect E symmetry, False for Perfect H.

tools.example:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("BoundarySetup")
oModule.AssignFEBI(["NAME:FEBI_outer", "Objects:=", ["Radome"]])
oModule.AssignHybridRegion(["NAME:PO_reflector", "Objects:=", ["Reflector"], "Type:=", "PO"])
cut = [int(f) for f in oEditor.GetFaceIDs("Region") if abs(float(oEditor.GetFaceCenter(int(f))[0])) < 1e-6]
oModule.AssignSymmetry(["NAME:SymH", "IsPerfectE:=", False, "Faces:=", cut])
oModule.SetImpedanceMultiplier(2)
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.assign_febi, hfss.assign_hybrid_region, hfss.assign_symmetry, hfss.set_impedance_multiplier. The impedance multiplier compensates port impedances cut by symmetry planes (oModule.SetImpedanceMultiplier).

tools.name: oModule("BoundarySetup").AssignLatticePair / AssignMaster / AssignSlave
tools.description: Periodic boundaries: AssignLatticePair couples two opposite faces of a rectangular unit cell with a phase delay given as scan angles, UV values or an explicit phase (2020 R1+), while AssignMaster / AssignSlave (Primary/Secondary in the GUI) define the general pair with explicit U vectors and are needed for skewed lattices. The phase-delay variables are what an Optimetrics scan sweep varies.
tools.usage:
oModule.AssignLatticePair(["NAME:LatticePair1", "Faces:=", [9, 8], "ReverseV:=", False, "PhaseDelay:=", "UseScanAngle", "Phi:=", "0deg", "Theta:=", "0deg"])
oModule.AssignLatticePair(["NAME:LatticePair2", "Faces:=", [8, 9], "ReverseV:=", False, "PhaseDelay:=", "InputPhaseDelay", "Phase:=", "10deg"])
oModule.AssignMaster(["NAME:Master1", "Faces:=", [10], ["NAME:CoordSysVector", "Origin:=", ["-p/2", "-p/2", "0mm"], "UPos:=", ["p/2", "-p/2", "0mm"]], "ReverseV:=", False])
oModule.AssignSlave(["NAME:Slave1", "Faces:=", [11], ["NAME:CoordSysVector", "Origin:=", ["-p/2", "p/2", "0mm"], "UPos:=", ["p/2", "p/2", "0mm"]], "ReverseV:=", False, "Master:=", "Master1", "UseScanAngles:=", True, "Phi:=", "0deg", "Theta:=", "0deg"])

parameters.name: Faces
parameters.description: Two face IDs for a lattice pair; one face for master or slave.

parameters.name: PhaseDelay
parameters.description: "UseScanAngle" (Phi/Theta), "UseScanUV" (U/V) or "InputPhaseDelay" (Phase).

parameters.name: CoordSysVector
parameters.description: Origin and UPos points on the face defining the U vector; V is derived.

parameters.name: Master / UseScanAngles / Phase
parameters.description: Slave references its master and carries the phase definition.

tools.example:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("BoundarySetup")
oModule.AssignLatticePair(["NAME:LatticeX", "Faces:=", [int(fx1), int(fx2)], "ReverseV:=", False, "PhaseDelay:=", "UseScanAngle",
                           "Phi:=", "phi_scan", "Theta:=", "theta_scan"])
oModule.AssignLatticePair(["NAME:LatticeY", "Faces:=", [int(fy1), int(fy2)], "ReverseV:=", False, "PhaseDelay:=", "UseScanAngle",
                           "Phi:=", "phi_scan", "Theta:=", "theta_scan"])
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.assign_lattice_pair / auto_assign_lattice_pairs / assign_primary / assign_secondary. The GUI labels changed to Primary/Secondary and Lattice Pair, but the script commands keep the Master/Slave names.

tools.name: oModule("BoundarySetup").AssignVoltage / AssignCurrent
tools.description: Ideal voltage and current source excitations on a sheet with a direction line, used when a structure should be driven with a fixed voltage/current instead of a port (field and radiation studies, transient drives). Magnitudes are set here and later weighted with EditSources.
tools.usage:
oModule.AssignVoltage(["NAME:Voltage1", "Voltage:=", "1000mV", ["NAME:Direction", "Start:=", ["-0.4mm", "-1.2mm", "0mm"], "End:=", ["-1.4mm", "-1.2mm", "0mm"]], "Faces:=", [7]])
oModule.AssignCurrent(["NAME:Current1", "Current:=", "1000mA", ["NAME:Direction", "Start:=", ["-0.4mm", "0.4mm", "-1.6mm"], "End:=", ["-0.4mm", "0.4mm", "0mm"]], "Faces:=", [12]])

parameters.name: Voltage / Current
parameters.description: Magnitude with units.

parameters.name: Direction
parameters.description: Start and End points on the sheet.

parameters.name: Faces / Objects
parameters.description: Sheet face ID or sheet object name.

tools.example:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("BoundarySetup")
oModule.AssignVoltage(["NAME:V1", "Voltage:=", "1V", ["NAME:Direction", "Start:=", ["0mm", "0mm", "0mm"], "End:=", ["0mm", "0mm", "h_gap"]], "Objects:=", ["VSheet"]])
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.assign_voltage_source_to_sheet / assign_current_source_to_sheet. Sources have no S-parameters; use Fields Calculator integrals for input impedance.

tools.name: oModule("BoundarySetup").AssignPlaneWave / AssignHertzianDipoleWave / AssignGaussianBeam
tools.description: Incident-wave excitations: a plane wave in Cartesian (E0 and k vectors) or spherical (phi/theta ranges with E-phi/E-theta) form with propagating/evanescent/elliptical options, a Hertzian dipole (electric or magnetic) at an origin with an exclusion sphere, and a Gaussian beam with beam width. All share the Faces list (usually the region's faces or omitted for the whole model) and the origin definition.
tools.usage:
oModule.AssignPlaneWave(["NAME:IncPWave1", "IsCartesian:=", True, "EoX:=", "1", "EoY:=", "0", "EoZ:=", "0", "kX:=", "0", "kY:=", "0", "kZ:=", "1",
    "OriginX:=", "0mm", "OriginY:=", "0mm", "OriginZ:=", "0mm", "IsPropagating:=", True, "IsEvanescent:=", False, "IsEllipticallyPolarized:=", False])
oModule.AssignPlaneWave(["NAME:IncPWave2", "IsCartesian:=", False, "PhiStart:=", "0deg", "PhiStop:=", "360deg", "PhiPoints:=", 73, "ThetaStart:=", "90deg", "ThetaStop:=", "90deg", "ThetaPoints:=", 1,
    "EoPhi:=", "0", "EoTheta:=", "1", "OriginX:=", "0mm", "OriginY:=", "0mm", "OriginZ:=", "0mm", "IsPropagating:=", True, "IsEvanescent:=", False, "IsEllipticallyPolarized:=", False])
oModule.AssignHertzianDipoleWave(["NAME:IncHDWave1", "IsCartesian:=", True, "EoX:=", "0", "EoY:=", "0", "EoZ:=", "1", "kX:=", "0", "kY:=", "0", "kZ:=", "1", "OriginX:=", "0mm", "OriginY:=", "0mm", "OriginZ:=", "0mm", "SphereRadius:=", "10mm", "IsElectricDipole:=", True])
oModule.AssignGaussianBeam(["NAME:IncGBeam1", "IsCartesian:=", True, "EoX:=", "1", "EoY:=", "0", "EoZ:=", "0", "kX:=", "0", "kY:=", "0", "kZ:=", "1", "OriginX:=", "0mm", "OriginY:=", "0mm", "OriginZ:=", "0mm", "BeamWidth:=", "10mm"])

parameters.name: IsCartesian
parameters.description: True = EoX/EoY/EoZ and kX/kY/kZ; False = spherical angle sweep with EoPhi/EoTheta.

parameters.name: PhiStart/Stop/Points, ThetaStart/Stop/Points
parameters.description: Incidence-angle sweep for monostatic RCS (each direction becomes an IWavePhi/IWaveTheta value).

parameters.name: IsPropagating / IsEvanescent / IsEllipticallyPolarized
parameters.description: Wave type flags; evanescent and elliptical add their own parameters (propagation constants, polarisation angle/ratio).

parameters.name: SphereRadius / IsElectricDipole
parameters.description: Hertzian dipole exclusion sphere and dipole type.

parameters.name: BeamWidth
parameters.description: Gaussian beam waist.

tools.example:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("BoundarySetup")
oModule.AssignPlaneWave(["NAME:IncPWave1", "IsCartesian:=", False, "PhiStart:=", "0deg", "PhiStop:=", "180deg", "PhiPoints:=", 181,
    "ThetaStart:=", "90deg", "ThetaStop:=", "90deg", "ThetaPoints:=", 1, "EoPhi:=", "0", "EoTheta:=", "1",
    "OriginX:=", "0mm", "OriginY:=", "0mm", "OriginZ:=", "0mm", "IsPropagating:=", True, "IsEvanescent:=", False, "IsEllipticallyPolarized:=", False])
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.plane_wave, hfss.hertzian_dipole_wave (Gaussian beam has no wrapper yet). Other incident waves: AssignLinearAntennaWave, AssignFarFieldWave, AssignNearFieldWave. Choose scattered vs total field with EditSources FieldType.

tools.name: oModule("BoundarySetup").AssignCircuitPort / AssignTerminal / AutoIdentifyPorts / AutoIdentifyTerminals
tools.description: Terminal-design and lumped-edge port commands: AssignCircuitPort creates a circuit port between two edges with impedance, renormalisation and de-embedding, AssignTerminal adds a terminal (edge on a conductor with a resistance) to an existing port, and AutoIdentifyPorts / AutoIdentifyTerminals let HFSS detect ports on given faces against reference conductors and create terminals automatically - the scripted Auto Assign Terminals.
tools.usage:
oModule.AssignCircuitPort(["NAME:CircuitPort1", "Edges:=", [36, 40], "Impedance:=", "50ohm", "DoDeembed:=", False, "RenormalizeAllTerminals:=", True])
oModule.AssignTerminal(["NAME:Rectangle1_T1", "Edges:=", [36], "ParentBndID:=", "WavePort1", "TerminalResistance:=", "50ohm"])
oModule.AutoIdentifyPorts(["NAME:Faces", 52], True, ["NAME:ReferenceConductors", "Gnd"], "P", True)
oModule.AutoIdentifyTerminals()

parameters.name: Edges
parameters.description: Two edge IDs (signal, reference) for a circuit port; one edge for a terminal.

parameters.name: ParentBndID / TerminalResistance
parameters.description: Owning port name and terminal reference resistance.

parameters.name: AutoIdentifyPorts arguments
parameters.description: Faces array, IsWavePort (True wave / False lumped), ReferenceConductors array, base name for created ports, UseConductorNames flag.

tools.example:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("BoundarySetup")
e_sig = int(oEditor.GetEdgeByPosition(["NAME:EdgeParameters", "BodyName:=", "Trace", "XPosition:=", "0mm", "YPosition:=", "0mm", "ZPosition:=", "h"]))
e_gnd = int(oEditor.GetEdgeByPosition(["NAME:EdgeParameters", "BodyName:=", "Gnd", "XPosition:=", "0mm", "YPosition:=", "0mm", "ZPosition:=", "0mm"]))
oModule.AssignCircuitPort(["NAME:P1", "Edges:=", [e_sig, e_gnd], "Impedance:=", "50ohm", "DoDeembed:=", False, "RenormalizeAllTerminals:=", True])

# terminal design: wave port on face 52 with Gnd as reference
oModule.AutoIdentifyPorts(["NAME:Faces", 52], True, ["NAME:ReferenceConductors", "Gnd"], "P", True)
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.circuit_port, hfss.wave_port(..., reference=...) which uses the reference conductor for terminals. AssignCircuitPort's exact key set varies by release; record once. Terminal designs require every port to have terminals or validation fails.

tools.name: oModule("BoundarySetup").EditWavePort / EditLumpedPort / EditPerfectE / EditFiniteCond / EditRadiation (Edit* commands)
tools.description: Every Assign* command has an Edit* counterpart taking the boundary name and a full replacement array, used to change modes, integration lines, impedance, de-embedding, materials or any other property of an existing boundary without deleting it. PyAEDT's BoundaryObject.update() issues exactly these calls.
tools.usage:
oModule.EditWavePort("WavePort1", ["NAME:WavePort1", "NumModes:=", 2, "PolarizeEField:=", False, "DoDeembed:=", True, "DeembedDist:=", "10mil", "DoRenorm:=", True, "RenormValue:=", "50Ohm",
    ["NAME:Modes", ["NAME:Mode1", "ModeNum:=", 1, "UseIntLine:=", True, ["NAME:IntLine", "Start:=", [-0.4, -1.2, 0], "End:=", [-1.4, 0.4, 0]], "CharImp:=", "Zpi"], ["NAME:Mode2", "ModeNum:=", 2, "UseIntLine:=", False]]])
oModule.EditLumpedPort("LumpPort1", ["NAME:LumpPort1", "Objects:=", ["Sheet1"], "DoDeembed:=", False, "RenormalizeAllTerminals:=", True, "Impedance:=", "50ohm", ...])
oModule.EditPerfectE("PerfE1", ["NAME:PerfE1", "Objects:=", ["Patch"], "InfGroundPlane:=", False])
oModule.EditFiniteCond("FiniteCond1", ["NAME:FiniteCond1", "Objects:=", [...], "UseMaterial:=", True, "Material:=", "copper", "UseThickness:=", False, "Roughness:=", "0um", "InfGroundPlane:=", False, "IsTwoSided:=", False, "IsInternal:=", True])
oModule.EditRadiation("Rad1", ["NAME:Rad1", "Objects:=", ["Region"]])

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Existing boundary name (case-sensitive).

parameters.name: array
parameters.description: Complete definition; the NAME inside may differ to rename the boundary.

parameters.name: CharImp
parameters.description: Wave-port mode impedance definition: "Zpi", "Zpv", "Zvi".

tools.example:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("BoundarySetup")
oModule.EditWavePort("P1", ["NAME:P1", "Faces:=", [int(face)], "NumModes:=", 1, "RenormalizeAllTerminals:=", True, "DoDeembed:=", True,
    "DeembedDist:=", "5mm", ["NAME:Modes", ["NAME:Mode1", "ModeNum:=", 1, "UseIntLine:=", True,
    ["NAME:IntLine", "Start:=", ["-L", "r_in", "0mm"], "End:=", ["-L", "r_out", "0mm"]], "AlignmentGroup:=", 0, "CharImp:=", "Zpi"]],
    "ShowReporterFilter:=", False, "ReporterFilter:=", [True], "UseAnalyticAlignment:=", False])
tools.notes: PyAEDT: bnd.props[...] = ...; bnd.update(). Read the current array with the ChildObject API (oDesign.GetChildObject("Boundaries").GetChildObject(name).GetPropValue(...)) or record an edit from the GUI to see the full key set of the installed release.

tools.name: oModule("BoundarySetup").DeleteBoundaries / DeleteAllBoundaries / ReassignBoundary / RenameBoundary / SetDiffPairs
tools.description: Boundary maintenance: delete named boundaries/excitations or all of them, move a boundary to other objects/faces, rename one, and define differential pairs of terminals with their mode names and reference impedances. Reassignment is the fix when geometry has been regenerated and face IDs changed.
tools.usage:
oModule.DeleteBoundaries(["PerfE1", "WavePort1"])
oModule.DeleteAllBoundaries()
oModule.ReassignBoundary(["NAME:PerfH12", "Faces:=", [17]])

oModule = oDesign.GetModule("AnalysisSetup")
oModule.InsertSetup("HfssEigen", ["NAME:Setup1", "MinimumFrequency:=", "1GHz", "NumModes:=", 3, "MaxDeltaFreq:=", 5, "ConvergeOnRealFreq:=", True,
    "MaximumPasses:=", 6, "MinimumPasses:=", 1, "MinimumConvergedPasses:=", 1, "PercentRefinement:=", 20, "IsEnabled:=", True, "BasisOrder:=", 1, "DoLambdaRefine:=", True, "DoMaterialLambda:=", True, "SetLambdaTarget:=", False, "Target:=", 0.2])

oModule.InsertSetup("HfssDrivenAuto", ["NAME:Setup1", "IsEnabled:=", True, "AutoSolverSetting:=", "Balanced", ["NAME:Sweeps", ["NAME:Sweep", "RangeType:=", "LinearCount", "RangeStart:=", "1GHz", "RangeEnd:=", "10GHz", "RangeCount:=", 501, "AutoSolverSetting:=", "Balanced", "Type:=", "Discrete"]]])

oModule = oDesign.GetModule("AnalysisSetup")

tools.description: Setup and sweep maintenance in the analysis module: modify an existing setup or sweep with a replacement array (any subset of keys, the rest unchanged), delete setups or a sweep, and list setup names and the sweeps of a setup. tools.usage:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("AnalysisSetup")
oModule.EditSetup("Setup1", ["NAME:Setup1", "Frequency:=", "5GHz", "MaxDeltaS:=", 0.01, "MaximumPasses:=", 20, "IsEnabled:=", True])
oModule.EditFrequencySweep("Setup1", "Sweep1", ["NAME:Sweep1", "IsEnabled:=", True, "RangeType:=", "LinearCount", "RangeStart:=", "1GHz", "RangeEnd:=", "6GHz", "RangeCount", 501, "Type:=", "Interpolating", "SaveFields:=", False])

setups = oModule.GetSetups()
sweeps = oModule.GetSweeps("Setup1")

parameters.name: setup / sweep names
parameters.description: Existing names; the NAME inside the array can rename.

parameters.name: array
parameters.description: Only the keys given are changed (EditSetup) - unlike Assign/Edit boundary calls that replace everything.

oModule.EditSetup("Setup2", ["NAME:Setup2",

parameters.name: Params

oModule = oDesign.GetModule("AnalysisSetup")

parameters.description: "Quasi Newton", "Pattern Search", "Sequential Nonlinear Programming" (SNLP), "Sequential Mixed Integer NLP", "Genetic Algorithm", "MATLAB Optimizer", "Screening" ...

parameters.name: AnalysisStopOptions
parameters.description: Iteration count, elapsed time, slow improvement and gradient tolerance stop criteria.

parameters.name: Variables
parameters.description: Per-variable Min/Max/MinStep/MaxStep/focus range and manufacturable levels.

parameters.name: Goals
parameters.description: ReportType, Solution, SimValueContext (Domain, Context for far fields), Calculation, Ranges (Type "d" discrete / "r" range), Condition ("<=", ">=", "==", "Minimize", "Maximize"), GoalValue, Weight.

parameters.name: UpdateDesign / UpdateIteration
parameters.description: Write the best variable values back into the design every N iterations.

tools.example:
# usually recorded from Optimetrics > Add > Optimization and then parameterised; solve it with:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("Optimetrics")
oModule.SolveSetup("OptimizationSetup1")
print(oModule.GetSetupNames())
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.optimizations.add(...) with optimization_type "Optimization"/"Sensitivity"/"Statistical"/"DXDOE", SetupOpti.add_goal / add_variation. Variables must be enabled for the study type in their Properties (Include in Optimization/Sensitivity/Statistical) before the setup is solved.

tools.name: oModule("Optimetrics").SolveSetup / EditSetup / DeleteSetups / GetSetupNames / ExportParametricResults / ExportOptimetricsResult
tools.description: Run and manage Optimetrics setups: solve one setup (all its variations/iterations), edit or delete setups, list them, export the parametric results table (variation values plus calculations) to CSV/TAB/DAT/TXT, and export optimisation results. SolveSetup blocks until the study completes; oDesign.Analyze(setupName) with the Optimetrics setup name is equivalent.
tools.usage:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("Optimetrics")
oModule.SolveSetup("ParametricSetup1")
oModule.EditSetup("ParametricSetup1", ["NAME:ParametricSetup1", ...])
oModule.DeleteSetups(["ParametricSetup1"])
names = oModule.GetSetupNames()
oModule.ExportParametricResults("ParametricSetup1", "C:/exportdir/test.csv", False)
oModule.ExportOptimetricsResult("OptimizationSetup1", "C:/exportdir/opt.csv", "")

parameters.name: ExportParametricResults arguments
parameters.description: Setup name, output file (.csv/.tab/.dat/.txt), bOutputUnits (include units in values).

parameters.name: ExportOptimetricsResult arguments
parameters.description: Setup name, output file, and a variation filter string (empty for all).

tools.example:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("Optimetrics")
for s in oModule.GetSetupNames():
    oModule.SolveSetup(s)
    oModule.ExportParametricResults(s, "C:/work/" + s + ".csv", True)
tools.notes: PyAEDT: param.analyze(), hfss.export_parametric_results, hfss.parametrics.delete. Distributed solving of variations follows the active HPC configuration (Optimetrics variations distribution type).

tools.name: oModule("BoundarySetup").AssignRadiation with Options / AssignFiniteCond with roughness (Huray / Groisse) - extended arrays
tools.description: Extended forms of two already-catalogued assignments: the radiation boundary array can carry an IsIncidentField/IsFssReference flag set and the 'Use Adaptive Radiation' options, and the finite-conductivity array supports surface roughness models - Groisse with a roughness RMS, or Huray with nodule radius and surface ratio - plus thickness for DC conductivity correction, two-sided sheets and internal/external side selection. Roughness raises conductor loss at high frequency for realistic PCB copper.
tools.usage:
oModule.AssignFiniteCond(["NAME:CuRough", "Objects:=", ["Trace"], "UseMaterial:=", True, "Material:=", "copper", "UseThickness:=", True, "Thickness:=", "35um",
    "Roughness:=", "1um", "InfGroundPlane:=", False, "IsTwoSided:=", False, "IsInternal:=", True,
    "RoughnessModel:=", "Huray", "NoduleRadius:=", "0.5um", "HallHuraySurfaceRatio:=", "2.9"])
oModule.AssignRadiation(["NAME:Rad1", "Objects:=", ["Region"], "IsIncidentField:=", False, "IsEnforcedField:=", False, "IsFssReference:=", False, "IsForPML:=", False, "UseAdaptiveIE:=", False, "IncludeInPostproc:=", True])

parameters.name: UseMaterial / Material / Conductivity / Permeability
parameters.description: Take conductivity from a material or give explicit values.

parameters.name: UseThickness / Thickness
parameters.description: Metal thickness used for the DC/low-frequency correction of the surface impedance.

parameters.name: Roughness / RoughnessModel / NoduleRadius / HallHuraySurfaceRatio
parameters.description: Groisse RMS roughness, or the Huray (Hall-Huray) model with snowball radius and surface ratio.

parameters.name: IsTwoSided / IsInternal
parameters.description: Sheet with fields on both sides, and which side the impedance applies to.

parameters.name: IncludeInPostproc
parameters.description: Radiation faces contribute to far-field computation.

tools.example:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("BoundarySetup")
cu_faces = [int(f) for o in oEditor.GetObjectsInGroup("copper") for f in oEditor.GetFaceIDs(o)]
oModule.AssignFiniteCond(["NAME:CuHuray", "Faces:=", cu_faces, "UseMaterial:=", True, "Material:=", "copper", "UseThickness:=", True,
    "Thickness:=", "35um", "Roughness:=", "0um", "InfGroundPlane:=", False, "IsTwoSided:=", False, "IsInternal:=", True,
    "RoughnessModel:=", "Huray", "NoduleRadius:=", "0.5um", "HallHuraySurfaceRatio:=", "2.9"])
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.assign_finite_conductivity(assignment, material, use_thickness, thickness, roughness, is_infinite_ground, is_two_side, is_internal, name) - the Huray keys are set through the returned BoundaryObject.props. Roughness model key names should be confirmed by recording on the installed release.
